subject: IT Tip of the week: How to organize your Outlook inbox
urls: False
attachments: False
sentiment: helpful, informative
->
completion:
body: This week's IT tip was provided by Tracy Van Devel.  Thanks, Tracy!


"Hi, I wanted to pass on a few tips to help everyone maintain a manageable email inbox.

First, I recommend using folders to organize your email.  You can create folders by 
clicking on File and select New Folder.  I have many folders such as "IT Correspondence", 
"Personal" etc.  I like to save all email correspondence that is sent from the same person 
and place it in a folder named after the individual.

Secondly, I set up a vacation email response.  This can be set up by going into Tools, 
then select Rules of Folders.  In the "Reply to External Contacts" option, type the 
message that you would like to be sent to external contacts.  For example: "I will be out of the 
office on vacation and will not be returning to the office until <DATE>.  Please contact me 
at that time for assistance."  This option allows your email to respond automatically with 
your response when someone is sending you an email.  Please note:  This option only applies to 
external email.  I think this option is great because it lets your co-workers know you are 
out of the office without having to forward them an email, or ask your co-workers to check your 
email for you, and it also tells the external contacts to contact you at a later date.

This third and final tip may not apply to everyone but I wanted to add it on.  I have 2 email 
addresses, <EMAIL> and <EMAIL>.  My <EMAIL> address is used for outside companies, 
co-workers and other external contacts.
